description: Given the head of a singly linked list, group all the nodes with odd indices together followed by the nodes with even indices. The first node is considered odd. Maintain relative order within each group.
intuition: Visualize splitting a chain into two interleaved chains (odd and even positions), then reconnecting them. Two pointers alternate through the list, each building their own sub-chain. Finally, attach the even chain to the end of the odd chain.
approach: Use two pointers: odd and even. Alternate linking: odd.next = odd.next.next and even.next = even.next.next. After traversal, connect the odd list to the even list head.
code:
class Solution:
    def oddEvenList(self, head):
        if not head:
            return head
        odd = head
        even = head.next
        even_head = even
        while even and even.next:
            odd.next = even.next
            odd = odd.next
            even.next = odd.next
            even = even.next
        odd.next = even_head
        return head
jsWalkthrough:
Example: head = [1,2,3,4,5]
oddTail=1, evenTail=2, evenHead=2

Iteration 1: evenTail=2, evenTail.next=3 → proceed
  oddTail.next = 3, oddTail = 3
  evenTail.next = 4, evenTail = 4
  List so far (odd chain): 1→3→4(temp), even chain: 2→4

Iteration 2: evenTail=4, evenTail.next=5 → proceed
  oddTail.next = 5, oddTail = 5
  evenTail.next = null, evenTail = null
  Odd chain: 1→3→5, even chain: 2→4→null

Connect: oddTail(5).next = evenHead(2)
Result: 1→3→5→2→4
explanation:
1. Initialize odd pointer at head and even pointer at head.next.
2. Save even_head to reconnect later.
3. Alternate: link odd to the next odd, then even to the next even.
4. After the loop, connect the end of the odd list to even_head.
hints: Separate the list into odd-indexed and even-indexed sublists.
Track the head of the even sublist to reconnect at the end.
Be careful with the termination condition of the while loop.
